items.stem: State any three characteristics of entrepreneurship.
items.answer: Systematic activity; Lawful and purposeful activity; Innovation; Organisation of production; Risk-taking
items.markingKey: Any three of: Systematic activity; Lawful and purposeful activity; Innovation; Organisation of production; Risk-taking (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following is true of entrepreneurship but not of employment?
items.answer: Capital: needed
items.markingKey: (d) entrepreneurship: Capital: needed. The other options describe employment.
options: Reward: salary or wages, which are fixed

items.stem: Explain the following action points of the Startup India scheme: (i) Funding support and incentives (ii) Industry-academia partnership and incubation.
items.answer: (i) Funding support and incentives: A fund of funds and tax benefits for eligible startups. (ii) Industry-academia partnership and incubation: Incubators and research parks in academic institutions.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) A fund of funds and tax benefits for eligible startups. (ii) Incubators and research parks in academic institutions.

items.stem: Meera's startup got office space, mentoring and seed money from a centre run by an engineering college. How is the startup being funded?
items.answer: Business incubators
items.markingKey: (d) Business incubators. Incubators support early-stage startups.

items.stem: Sahil put all his savings into a new venture knowing it might fail. Which characteristic of entrepreneurship is shown? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Risk-taking. The entrepreneur bears the risk.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Risk-taking; 2 marks for the justification: The entrepreneur bears the risk.

items.stem:
Tara, an engineering student in Mumbai, has an idea for a solar-powered water pump. She has little money and no business experience.
(i) Suggest two ways she could fund the startup. (ii) How can Startup India help?
items.answer: (i) Bootstrapping, crowdfunding, angel investors, incubators (any two). (ii) Simplified compliance and handholding, funding support, incubation through industry-academia partnership.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Bootstrapping, crowdfunding, angel investors, incubators (any two). (ii) Simplified compliance and handholding, funding support, incubation through industry-academia partnership.

items.stem: Karthik attended a training course to learn how to plan and run a business before starting one. Which characteristic of entrepreneurship is shown?
items.answer: Systematic activity
items.markingKey: (a) Systematic activity. Entrepreneurship needs skills that can be learnt.

items.stem: Harpreet invented a low-cost water filter and started selling it in villages near Mumbai. Which characteristic of entrepreneurship is shown?
items.answer: Innovation
items.markingKey: (c) Innovation. A new product creates value.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about entrepreneurship and Startup India is correct?
items.answer: Innovation is a characteristic of entrepreneurship.
items.markingKey: (a) Correct: Innovation is a characteristic of entrepreneurship.
options: Innovation is a characteristic of entrepreneurship.
Startup India was launched to support only foreign companies.
Angel investors are banks that give loans to startups.

items.stem: A professionally managed fund invested ₹20 crore in Sharma Retail because of its high growth potential. How is the startup being funded?
items.answer: Venture capital
items.markingKey: (b) Venture capital. Professional funds investing for equity.

items.stem:
Kunal left a salaried job to start Sharma Retail, which makes eco-friendly packaging from farm waste.
(i) Compare his old and new occupations on reward and risk. (ii) Identify two characteristics of entrepreneurship in the case. (iii) How does such enterprise help the economy?
items.answer: (i) Employment: fixed salary, little risk. Entrepreneurship: uncertain profit, risk is borne. (ii) Innovation (new product from waste), risk-taking, organisation of production (any two). (iii) Creates jobs, adds to national income, reduces waste, balanced regional development.
items.markingKey: 6 marks: (i) Employment: fixed salary, little risk. Entrepreneurship: uncertain profit, risk is borne. (ii) Innovation (new product from waste), risk-taking, organisation of production (any two). (iii) Creates jobs, adds to national income, reduces waste, balanced regional development.

items.stem: State any three roles of small business in India.
items.answer: Large source of employment; Balanced regional development; Wide variety of products; Contribution to exports; Support to large industries; Opportunities for entrepreneurship; Low cost of production; Quick decision-making and personalised service
items.markingKey: Any three of: Large source of employment; Balanced regional development; Wide variety of products; Contribution to exports; Support to large industries; Opportunities for entrepreneurship; Low cost of production; Quick decision-making and personalised service (1 mark each).

items.stem: Explain the following roles of small business in India: (i) Large source of employment (ii) Quick decision-making and personalised service.
items.answer: (i) Large source of employment: Small industries are the second largest employer after agriculture. (ii) Quick decision-making and personalised service: Small size allows flexibility and close contact with customers.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Small industries are the second largest employer after agriculture. (ii) Small size allows flexibility and close contact with customers.

items.stem: Explain the following roles of small business in rural areas: (i) Reduces migration to cities (ii) Use of local resources and skills.
items.answer: (i) Reduces migration to cities: Rural jobs check movement to towns. (ii) Use of local resources and skills: Local raw materials and crafts are used.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Rural jobs check movement to towns. (ii) Local raw materials and crafts are used.

items.stem: Thousands of small handicrafts units together employ more people than the few large factories in Dehradun. Which role of small business is illustrated?
items.answer: Large source of employment
items.markingKey: (c) Large source of employment. Small business is labour intensive.

items.stem: A small unit uses local materials and has low overheads, so it sells at lower prices than big brands. Which role of small business is illustrated? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Low cost of production. Local resources and low overheads cut costs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Low cost of production; 2 marks for the justification: Local resources and low overheads cut costs.

items.stem: Which role of small business is illustrated? In each case give a reason. (i) Handicraft units of Lucknow sell most of their output to buyers abroad. (ii) Thousands of small bicycles units together employ more people than the few large factories in Lucknow.
items.answer: (i) Contribution to exports: Small units earn foreign exchange. (ii) Large source of employment: Small business is labour intensive.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Contribution to exports (ii) Large source of employment

items.stem:
The government of a state plans to promote small units in its backward districts rather than one large steel plant.
(i) Give two reasons why small units suit this aim. (ii) Name one problem these units may face.
items.answer: (i) They create more jobs per rupee of capital; they can be set up in rural and backward areas (balanced regional development); they use local resources. (ii) Finance, raw materials, marketing, managerial skill, technology (any one).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) They create more jobs per rupee of capital; they can be set up in rural and backward areas (balanced regional development); they use local resources. (ii) Finance, raw materials, marketing, managerial skill, technology (any one).

items.stem:
Zoya makes handloom sarees at home in a village near Patna with the help of her family, using simple looms.
(i) What kind of industry is this? Give two features. (ii) State two ways such industries help rural areas. (iii) Suggest one form of help Zoya could seek.
items.answer: (i) Cottage industry: family labour, simple equipment, small capital, made at home (any two). (ii) Rural employment, reduced migration, use of local skills, higher rural incomes (any two). (iii) Credit from banks or NABARD-supported schemes; marketing help from government agencies; training through the DIC.
items.markingKey: 6 marks: (i) Cottage industry: family labour, simple equipment, small capital, made at home (any two). (ii) Rural employment, reduced migration, use of local skills, higher rural incomes (any two). (iii) Credit from banks or NABARD-supported schemes; marketing help from government agencies; training through the DIC.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about small business in India is correct?
items.answer: Small industries are an important source of employment.
items.markingKey: (d) Correct: Small industries are an important source of employment.
options: Small industries make no contribution to exports.
Ancillary units compete with large industries and never supply them.
Small industries cannot be set up in rural areas.
Small industries are an important source of employment.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Ancillary unit"?
items.answer: A small unit that supplies parts and components to a large industry.
items.markingKey: (a) Ancillary unit: A small unit that supplies parts and components to a large industry.
options: A small unit that supplies parts and components to a large industry.
Industries organised by individuals with private resources, using family labour and simple equipment, often at home.

The law that defines micro, small and medium enterprises in India and provides for their promotion and development.

items.answer: Employment in rural areas; Reduces migration to cities; Use of local resources and skills; Increases rural incomes
items.markingKey: Any three of: Employment in rural areas; Reduces migration to cities; Use of local resources and skills; Increases rural incomes (1 mark each).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Small units can give personalised service to customers.
Reason (R): Small units are in close contact with their customers.

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both true and R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.

items.stem: What is meant by "DIC"?
items.answer: District Industries Centre, the institution at the district level that provides all services and support to small entrepreneurs under a single roof.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: District Industries Centre, the institution at the district level that provides all services and support to small entrepreneurs under a single roof.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about problems of small business and government assistance is NOT correct?
items.answer: Small units never face competition from large firms.

options: Small units often depend on middlemen for marketing.
DICs provide support to small entrepreneurs at the district level.
Small units never face competition from large firms.
NSIC supplies machines to small units on hire-purchase.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): NSIC helps small units in exporting.
Reason (R): NSIC was set up to regulate the stock market.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true; R is false: it was set up to promote small industries.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.answer: Raw materials
items.markingKey: (d) Raw materials. Small purchases mean high prices and poor quality.

items.stem: Saxena and Sons buys inputs in small lots and pays more than large firms for poorer quality. Which problem of small business is it? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Raw materials. Small purchases mean high prices and poor quality.

items.stem:
Rahul runs a small furniture unit near Bhopal. He faces three problems: no bank will lend to him, his machines are old, and he sells only through middlemen.
(i) Name the three problems. (ii) Suggest an institution for each.
items.answer: (i) Finance, technology and marketing. (ii) Finance: SIDBI or DIC help with bank credit; technology: NSIC technology support or hire-purchase of machines; marketing: NSIC marketing support.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Finance, technology and marketing. (ii) Finance: SIDBI or DIC help with bank credit; technology: NSIC technology support or hire-purchase of machines; marketing: NSIC marketing support.

items.stem: Ishita wants advice, a feasibility report and help with a bank loan, all at one office in her district. Which institution would help?
items.answer: DIC
items.markingKey: (a) DIC. The DIC provides support to small entrepreneurs at the district level under one roof.

items.answer: (i) The DIC: it identifies entrepreneurs, prepares feasibility reports, arranges credit and marketing at the district level. (ii) NSIC: machines on hire-purchase, marketing; NABARD: rural credit; SIDBI: finance for small industry (any two).

items.stem:
Om has started Jain Industries, which sells herbal skin-care products under a new brand name. He has also invented a new extraction machine and written a recipe book.

items.answer: (i) Brand name: trademark; machine: patent; book: copyright. (ii) They prevent copying, reward creativity, build brand value and encourage further research.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Brand name: trademark; machine: patent; book: copyright. (ii) They prevent copying, reward creativity, build brand value and encourage further research.

items.stem: Explain the following reasons why IPR matters to entrepreneurs: (i) Encourages investment in research (ii) Builds brand value.
items.answer: (i) Encourages investment in research: Firms are willing to spend on innovation. (ii) Builds brand value: Protected trademarks build goodwill.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Firms are willing to spend on innovation. (ii) Protected trademarks build goodwill.

items.stem: Pillai Retail registers the name and logo under which it sells its organic food products. Which type of intellectual property right protects it?
items.answer: Trademark
items.markingKey: (b) Trademark. Brand names and logos are trademarks.

items.stem: Explain the following features of cottage industries: (i) Organised by individuals with private resources (ii) Simple equipment.
items.answer: (i) Organised by individuals with private resources: The owner provides the capital. (ii) Simple equipment: Simple tools are used.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) The owner provides the capital. (ii) Simple tools are used.

items.stem:
Rahul, an engineering student in Agra, has an idea for a solar-powered water pump. He has little money and no business experience.
(i) Suggest two ways he could fund the startup. (ii) How can Startup India help?
items.answer: (i) Bootstrapping, crowdfunding, angel investors, incubators (any two). (ii) Simplified compliance and handholding, funding support, incubation through industry-academia partnership.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Bootstrapping, crowdfunding, angel investors, incubators (any two). (ii) Simplified compliance and handholding, funding support, incubation through industry-academia partnership.

items.stem: Aditi put all her savings into a new venture knowing it might fail. Which characteristic of entrepreneurship is shown?
items.answer: Risk-taking
items.markingKey: (c) Risk-taking. The entrepreneur bears the risk.

items.stem: Which term relating to small business is described here? "Industries organised by individuals with private resources, using family labour and simple equipment, often at home."
items.answer: Cottage industries
items.markingKey: (b) Cottage industries: Industries organised by individuals with private resources, using family labour and simple equipment, often at home.
